chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the hunting of the Magian for the fish when they strike with the net and do not name (God), and similarly the Jew. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem. Rather, the hunting of the fish is seizing it.'
ai.seo_question: Is fish caught by non-Muslims without reciting Bismillah permissible in Bismillah halal?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that fish caught by People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) is permissible even without the recitation of Bismillah, distinguishing their practice from that of Muslims. This ruling is grounded in the specific definition of hunting fish as mere capture (akhdh), which does not require the ritual invocation necessary for land animals. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the rules of slaughter and hunting vary significantly based on the nature of the animal.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about hunting of the Magians for the fish when they catch it by the net, and they are not Naming (Bismillah), and similar to that are the Jews. So heasws said: ‘There is no problem. But rather, hunting the fishes it seizing it’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from abu Basir who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about fishing by Zoroastrian and Jews by means of fishing nets without a mention of the name of Allah. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful, fishing is to catch it alive.’”
